chunks: Humeed ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, from Al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Muhammad ibn Ziyad, both together, from Abdul-Rahman ibn Al-Hajjaj, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Similar to it, except that he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is established that what he left is insufficient to cover all his debt, then no expenditure should be made on them [the dependents], and if it is not established, then expenditure should be made on them from the middle of the wealth.'
ai.seo_question: How is a deceased person's estate distributed among dependents and creditors when the debt amount is uncertain?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi highlights the Shia juristic principle of balancing creditor rights with the maintenance of dependents (nafaqah), prioritizing certainty in debt settlement. It reflects the practical application of estate distribution where, in cases of ambiguous debt magnitude, the family's sustenance is secured from the 'middle' of the assets to ensure stability, a nuance distinct from some Sunni schools that may prioritize creditors more strictly. The hadith underscores the importance of distinguishing between certain and probable liabilities in Islamic inheritance law.

en.hubeali:
Hameed Bin iyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Al Husayn Bin Hashim and Muhammad Bin Ziyad, both together, from Abdul Rahman Al hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan,

similar to it except that he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he was convinced that, that which he has left would be encompassed by his debt, so he should not spend upon them, and if was not convinced, so let him spend over them from the middle of the wealth’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from Sama‘ah from al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Muhammad ibn Ziyad all from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj

who has narrated a similar Hadith except that he has said: ‘If it is certain that his legacy covers all of his debts then it is not spent on them but if it is not certain then from the center of the legacy their expenses are paid..’”
